metadata.title: Bare Metal Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Defines foundational trust assumptions for non-virtualized physical compute substrates on which all higher-level platforms depend.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Applies to physical servers, firmware, provisioning systems, and out-of-band management planes.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Establishes explicit trust boundaries at the point where software execution meets physical hardware.

metadata.remarks: Bare Metal Core defines the trust baseline for physical compute hosts prior to virtualization, containerization, or cloud abstraction. This pattern exists to avoid implicit assumptions about hardware integrity, provisioning, and control planes, and to make physical host trust an explicit, assertable capability.

components.title: Physical Host Integrity
components.description: Establishes expectations for the integrity and controlled lifecycle of physical compute hosts.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Physical hosts are managed, inventoried, and operated in a manner that supports trustworthy execution of software workloads.

components.title: Firmware and Boot Trust
components.description: Defines trust assumptions for firmware, boot processes, and early execution stages.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Firmware and boot processes are managed to reduce the risk of persistent or undetected compromise.

components.title: Out-of-Band Management Trust
components.description: Covers trust considerations for remote and out-of-band management interfaces.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Out-of-band management systems are treated as privileged control planes and governed accordingly.

components.title: Provisioning and Lifecycle Control
components.description: Addresses trust in host provisioning, re-imaging, and decommissioning processes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Provisioning and lifecycle workflows are designed to prevent unauthorized persistence and configuration drift.
